description: Canonical notifications layout-parity scenario (WS3 oracle, v0.1.9). The SINGLE source of truth for the shared fixture: both the legacy notifications.js client and the multiplexer render this same logical content, so any layout delta is attributable to CSS/DOM, never data (Doc 00 §3 Premise C; Doc 01 'The shared fixture'). Deterministic timestamps (pinned ISO-8601 UTC, exactly as the existing visual fixtures do) so goldens are byte-stable. Exercises the contract surfaces both clients already render: .sender-card (header / persona badge / active indicator / counts), .date-accordion (header / date-text / count / toggle / messages), .sender-message.incoming AND .sender-message.outgoing. The D3 responded pair (parity-responded-1 → incoming prompt + synthetic {id}-response outgoing bubble) puts .outgoing styling under the oracle from day one.
